title: Web APIs Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Web APIs course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What does JSON.parse produce?
questions.explanation: JSON is a text format for data. JSON.parse turns that text into JavaScript values that code can read.

questions.question: Why check response.ok?
options: A response can arrive with an error status
questions.explanation: fetch asks for a resource and returns a promise for a response. A successful connection can still return a status such as 404, so check ok.

questions.question: Which object sends the stop signal?
questions.explanation: AbortController gives a request a stop signal. It is useful when a page no longer needs a slow answer.

questions.question: What does params.get("topic") return?
questions.explanation: URLSearchParams reads and writes query values in an address. It handles the encoding of spaces and special characters.

questions.question: Why use JSON.stringify before storing the array?
options: It uploads the array to a server
questions.explanation: localStorage stores small text values for one site in one browser. Objects need to be turned into text first.

questions.question: Which file can this page read through the input?
options: Every private file on the computer
questions.explanation: A file input lets a person choose a file. The page can read that chosen file; it cannot freely browse every file on the computer.

questions.question: Why run the copy step from a button action?
options: Clipboard access may need a user gesture
questions.explanation: The Clipboard API can write text to the clipboard. It normally needs a secure page and a deliberate user action.

questions.question: Can the person refuse a location request?
options: No, every page always gets it
Yes, the page must handle that choice
questions.explanation: Geolocation asks the browser for a location. The person can refuse, and the answer may be approximate.

questions.question: Which command draws the filled rectangle?
questions.explanation: Canvas is a drawing area controlled by JavaScript. Its 2D context has commands for shapes and text.

questions.question: Why call unobserve after the first message?
options: Only one notification is needed in this example
questions.explanation: IntersectionObserver tells your code when an element crosses a visibility boundary. It avoids doing a manual scroll check on every scroll event.

questions.question: What does this observer measure?
options: The number of files on disk
questions.explanation: ResizeObserver reports changes to an element's size. This can help a chart fit its own box rather than the whole screen.

questions.question: How does the worker send its answer?
questions.explanation: A web worker runs JavaScript in another thread. It can do a calculation without directly changing the page DOM.
